compiled_state.description:
Follow-up from edeb-c3ad-c051-4e6a (closed duplicate; the active flake was fixed under e9d5/d46c332c by switching effect_spies from monkeypatch.setattr to patch.object).

LATENT (not active) fragility observed during the edeb investigation: the autouse `_network_guard` fixture installs its socket-connect guard via `patch.object` and relies on strict-LIFO teardown. If a FUTURE test/fixture patches `socket.socket.connect`/`connect_ex` via a mechanism that is not LIFO-aware (e.g. monkeypatch.setattr, whose dict-snapshot restore blindly setattrs), its teardown can silently re-install `_network_guard`'s guard permanently on the xdist worker, breaking every later @allow_network test with "Network access is forbidden". This is exactly the mechanism that caused edeb; it is currently dormant because effect_spies was fixed, but nothing structurally prevents a new patcher from re-seeding it.

This is OPTIONAL defense-in-depth, not a fix for a live defect. Scope is test-only.

Acceptance criteria (all observable, test-only):
1. `_network_guard` teardown restores the real socket.connect/connect_ex regardless of intervening non-LIFO patching (self-healing: it captures and restores the true original, not whatever is currently installed).
2. A RED regression test reproduces the non-LIFO re-seed (a monkeypatch-style patch layered over the active guard) and asserts a later @allow_network path still reaches the real socket — RED before the change, GREEN after.
3. No change to production (non-test) code.
4. Full unit suite passes under xdist (no isolation regressions).

Escalation: whether to invest in this now vs leave filed is an operator call (flagged). Design decision if the self-healing approach turns out to require changing the guard's public contract.
compiled_state.title: Defense-in-depth: make _network_guard self-healing against non-LIFO patchers
